cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: test coverage sits at 31%, there is no coverage gate in continuous integration, and production systems of comparable complexity typically run 40-60% coverage.
cases.output: Test coverage sits at 31%, with no coverage gate in continuous integration. Production systems of comparable complexity typically run 40 to 60% coverage. Without a gate, regressions can reach production unchallenged, and the team lacks visibility into which code paths lack testing.

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: deployments are performed manually by one engineer via SSH, there is no rollback procedure, and the last rollback attempt (8 months ago) took over 3 hours to complete.
cases.output: The most recent rollback attempt, 8 months ago, took over 3 hours to complete, and deployments are performed manually by a single engineer via SSH with no documented rollback procedure. This creates a single point of failure in production availability, with no mitigation underway. A regression or misconfiguration can reach production unchallenged, and recovery depends entirely on one person's ability to diagnose and reverse the change under time pressure. We recommend automating deployments with a tested rollback path and distributing deployment authority across at least two engineers.

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: one engineer holds sole access to the production database credentials, there is no documented access-handover process, and that engineer is on a rolling month-to-month contract.
cases.output: Production database credentials are held by a single engineer on a month-to-month contract, with no documented access-handover process. If that engineer's contract ends or is terminated, the company loses database access entirely and has no procedure to recover it. There is no compensating control. This is a critical dependency on a single person with no mitigation underway.

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: customer personal data is retained indefinitely with no deletion policy, and there is no documented process for handling a data-subject deletion request.
cases.output: Customer personal data is retained indefinitely with no documented deletion policy. The company has no process to handle data-subject deletion requests, which creates exposure under GDPR, CCPA, and similar regulations. This is a control that exists on paper—retention obligations are mentioned in privacy documentation—and has never been exercised. We recommend establishing a data retention schedule with defined periods per data category, implementing a documented workflow for deletion requests, and testing the workflow quarterly with a sample of past requests.

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) covering ALL of these facts: test coverage is 31%, there is no CI coverage gate, the last three production incidents were caused by untested edge cases, deployments are manual, and there is no rollback procedure. Do not omit any fact.
cases.output: Test coverage sits at 31%, with no coverage gate in continuous integration. The last 3 production incidents originated in untested edge cases. Deployments are performed manually with no documented rollback procedure. This combination means a regression can reach production unchallenged and, once there, cannot be reliably reversed.

cases.input: Write three separate due-diligence findings, one paragraph each, clearly separated by a blank line. Finding 1 facts: passwords are stored in plaintext in the users table. Finding 2 facts: deployments are manual with no rollback procedure. Finding 3 facts: code comment style is inconsistent across the codebase, with no linting rule enforcing a convention.
cases.output:
Passwords are stored in plaintext in the users table with no hashing or encryption applied. This creates a critical exposure: any compromise of the database immediately yields valid credentials for every user account, and an attacker needs no further work to gain authenticated access to the application and any systems where users reuse those passwords. No compensating control limits who can access the database or what an intruder can do once inside.

Deployments are performed manually via SSH by individual engineers with no documented rollback procedure. The last attempted rollback, 14 months ago, took 6 hours to complete and required three engineers to coordinate the revert. This is a significant risk because a failed production deployment has no practiced path back to a working state, and the time to recover grows with the size of the change and the number of engineers involved.

Code comment style varies throughout the codebase with no enforced convention. Developers use inline comments, block comments, and no comments at all for similar patterns, and no linting rule exists to standardize the approach. This is a mild finding at the company's current stage: new team members spend extra time inferring intent from inconsistent documentation, but the lack of convention does not block understanding and a linter rule can be added without rework to existing code.
